newsitem.title: USA: US Northeast spot power prices extend recent gain.
newsitem.headline: US Northeast spot power prices extend recent gain.

text.p: Day-ahead bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Northeast extended Tuesday their recent gain due to outlook of frigid temperatures and outages of several large nuclear power plants in the region.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Wednesday delivery in the eastern half of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) edged up to $32.00-$33.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Monday's $31.50-$32.50 for delivery today.
Off-peak, non-firm power for day-ahead delivery in eastern NYPP was again assessed near $24.00. "But you'll have a problem finding any," said a Houston power marketer.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Wednesday held in a $26.00-$27.00 range.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Wednesday firmed to $17.50-$18.50 from $15.00-$18.00 Monday.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border was steady at $33.00-$35.00, almost unchanged from Monday's $33.00-$35.50.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for day-ahead delivery at the NU border was quoted near $24.00, the upper end of Monday's range.
Forecasts showed temperatures would trend lower the rest of the week with chances of snow Thursday. Readings would average well below normal throughout the region Friday and Saturday.

The 832 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick plant in Scriba, N.Y., began restart today after being taken off line last week to remove fish and debris accumulated on screens in water intakes that supply cooling water to the plant.

The two units at the Indian Point nuclear generating complex north of New York City remained shut. The 975 MW unit 2, which was shut Sunday to correct problems with a feedwater valve. was scheduled to start later this week. The 965 MW unit 3 was expected to stay idled through mid-February for replacement work in its primary containment area.
"We're going to see units coming on the next few days. You'll see prices stablize," said a New York power trader.
Swing natural gas values at the New York City gate strengthened to $3.60 per million British thermal units, up 20 cents from Monday's level.
